Grant Hardie Leads Scotland to Record-Equalling Gold at European Curling Championships

02 Nov 2026, 12:13 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

A Historic Victory in Ostrava

Grant Hardie has secured his fifth European Curling Championship gold medal, leading his Scottish rink to a narrow 6-5 victory over Italy in the final held in Ostrava, Czech Republic. This win marks a significant milestone for Hardie, who matches the record for the most European gold medals held by a Scottish curler, joining Mike Hay and Hammy McMillan Sr. in the history books.

Hardie’s success in Ostrava continues an impressive run of form, as he has now earned a medal in every one of his seven appearances at the European Championships.

Key Moments from the Men's Final

The final was defined by a tactical exchange between Scotland and Italy, who had previously handed the Scots their only loss during the group stage. Notable highlights included:

  • Early Consistency: The two teams remained closely matched throughout the opening seven ends.
  • Crucial Advantage: A steal of two points in the fourth end proved pivotal for the Scottish side.
  • The Deciding Score: Scotland secured the decisive point in the eighth end, confirming their status as pre-tournament favorites.

Following the match, Hardie expressed his satisfaction with the team's progression throughout the week, noting that the squad improved with each consecutive game.

Women's Rink Falls Short of Bronze

While the men celebrated gold, it was a challenging day for the Scottish women’s rink led by Fay Henderson. Competing for the bronze medal, the Scottish side faced a surging Latvian team that ultimately secured an 8-6 victory. This win for Latvia represents their first-ever major medal in the sport.

The match dynamics were intense, with Latvia building an early four-point lead. Although Scotland managed a significant three-point gain in the fourth end and a two-point success in the final end, they were unable to overcome the gap established during the middle stages of the match.
